references.text: Jesus asks the healed blind man if he believes in the Son of Man, which creates the direct context for the man's question about who He is.
Nathanael asks Jesus a similar question: "Rabbi, you are God's Son, you are the King of Israel," and confirms his faith after receiving revelation about who Jesus is.

Peter answers Jesus' question about whether the disciples will leave Him by confessing: "You have the words of eternal life. We have believed and know that you are the Holy One of God," which mirrors the man's willingness to believe when he learns who Jesus is.

Jesus explains that whoever believes in Him believes in the Father who sent Him, and that whoever sees Him sees the Father, providing the theological answer to the man's question about whom he should believe.
Jesus says: "Believe in God; believe also in me," which is the direct invitation responding to the man's search for someone to believe in.
Jesus defines eternal life as knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ, whom He has sent, which is at the heart of the man's question about identity and faith.
